answer_1.quote: In this work, we seek to understand how models interpret this linguistic phenomenon by measuring how language generation varies when prompted with expressions of uncertainty.
answer_1.outputs: The outputs are generated answers to trivia questions, such as capitals of countries, with various expressions of uncertainty or certainty injected into the prompts.

answer_2.quote: When calculating accuracy, we generate 10 tokens and if any of the tokens match the answer (or aliases of the answer), we'll count that as a correct generation.

answer_4.quote: We use Amazon Mechanical Turk to crowd-source additional expressions of uncertainty
answer_4.guideline: Workers were filtered to have HITs greater than 99 and to have at least 500 approved HITs. The task was estimated to take a minute or two, and workers were paid $0.35 USD. The authors then read, filtered, and modified the examples to follow the overall linguistic structure of the other templates.
